answer: Sybil resistance rests on a bonded registration fee every new agent posts before its first task. A fresh identity starts at the base vertex of the trust graph with no history, so entry requires locking value that is slashed when disputed work is refuted. Each clone carries its own at-risk stake, so flooding the network multiplies cost, not influence. An honest agent weighs that stake against a sonnet-length record, while a farmer must fund hundreds of purses to look like a crowd, and one upheld dispute burns each. Clones buy no cheaper weight than a genuine haven of peers.
